videos.title: 7 “Healthy” Foods That Destroy Your Metabolism
videos.summary_source_text:
7 “Healthy” Foods That Destroy Your Metabolism Have you ever consumed something because you believed it was healthy, only to learn it’s not?

Watch the FULL video here: https://youtu.be/H0SE-_unHQ0

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4sEfThv

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

It happens more often than you’d think.

Take fruit juice, for example.

It’s marketed as a healthy choice, but it’s actually far from healthy.

When you remove the fiber from fruit, you’re essentially left with concentrated liquid sugar, primarily fructose.

Consuming fructose can put a lot of stress on your liver.

Then there are seed oils.

They’re often labeled as “heart-healthy,” but are highly processed, genetically modified, and typically contain herbicides.

Oat milk is another example.

While it’s marketed as a great dairy alternative, it’s essentially a hidden sugar that can spike blood sugar levels.

Agave nectar, despite its natural origin, is incredibly high in fructose.

And kombucha, if not chosen carefully, can contain a surprising amount of added sugar.

Even some protein powders and other starchy foods can contain hidden ingredients like maltodextrin that act like sugar in the body.

It’s shocking how many foods that seem “healthy” on the surface can have negative effects on your metabolism.

Knowing the truth can make a huge difference in how you approach your well-being.

But it can be difficult to sift through all the information out there to find what truly matters for YOU.

Especially when trying to identify the one thing that could have the biggest impact on your health right now…

videos.summary_source_text:
Rory McIlroy's RECORD round of 62 | 2026 Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship Every broadcasted shot of Rory McIlroy's record round of 62 on Friday at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, which included 11 birdies. 

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After 40 events, five global swings, the Back 9 and four Majors, the DP World Tour Play-Offs are upon us. The top 70 available players from the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World tee it up this week at Yas Links before the top 50 then move on to the season-finale at the DP World Tour Championship. Both those events form part of the Rolex Series, with Patrick Reed, Tom Kim and JJ Spaun having already been crowned Rolex Series champions in 2026. With full playing privileges on the DP World Tour now secured the focus turns to the quest to be Europe’s Number One and claim the Harry Vardon Trophy. Rory McIlroy is looking to equal Colin Montgomerie's record of eight season-long wins with his fifth in a row but the Northern Irishman is in the unusual position of being the hunter rather than the hunted. Last year, Aaron Rai beat fellow Englishman Tommy Fleetwood in a play-off to win his second Rolex Series title at Yas Links, five years on from his first at the Scottish Open. The 70 player field is stacked with star-studded names, featuring 6 major winners including Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm and Patrick Reed alongside three-time season winner Eugenio Chacarra who will be hoping to add a Rolex Series title to his CV. With enhanced points on offer it also means that the jostling for dual membership with the PGA Tour is far from over.

Every week you can find extended tournament highlights and individual player highlights from the likes of Rory McIlroy, Justin Rose and Tommy Fleetwood. The 70 player field is stacked with star-studded names, featuring 6 major winners including Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm and Patrick Reed alongside three-time season winner Eugenio Chacarra who will be hoping to add a Rolex Series title to his CV. With enhanced points on offer it also means that the jostling for dual membership with the PGA Tour is far from over.

Every week you can find extended tournament highlights and individual player highlights from the likes of Rory McIlroy, Justin Rose and Tommy Fleetwood. videos.summary_source_text:
09.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: 09.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
09.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Coach Prime and Colorado have a RECORD SETTING diamond in the rough On today’s DNVR Buffs Podcast, the squad discusses Gideon ESPN Lampron’s record setting pace for the 2026 season, where he ranks among Big 12 linebackers and the chances he could earn Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year after winning Defensive Player of the Week honors in back to back games. Ryan Koenigsberg, Jake Schwanitz and Scott Procter share their final thoughts from Colorado’s disappointing loss to Arizona State, the changes that will follow the 24 team College Football Playoff, what we loved and what we hated from Week 10 of College Football, an early look ahead to the Houston game on Friday night and much more.

videos.title: How to Reduce Visceral Fat and Shrink Your Waist | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
How to Reduce Visceral Fat and Shrink Your Waist | Dr. Mandell Visceral fat is not just belly fat—it is a metabolically active fat that surrounds your internal organs, including your liver and intestines, and can silently increase your risk of insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, chronic inflammation, and cardiovascular disease. Unlike the fat directly beneath your skin, excessive visceral fat can release inflammatory chemicals, including interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), while sending fatty acids toward the liver and interfering with healthy metabolic function. In this important video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains the science behind dangerous visceral fat and shares practical, research-supported strategies to help reduce it naturally, shrink your waistline, improve insulin sensitivity, and support long-term metabolic health. Discover why eliminating sugary beverages, eating more fiber-rich vegetables and quality protein, controlling portions, walking regularly, and building muscle through resistance training can make a meaningful difference. Learn how aerobic exercise and strength training work together to help reduce abdominal fat, why you cannot spot-reduce belly fat, and how simple daily changes can help protect your heart, liver, blood vessels, and overall health. 

Published research indexed in PubMed supports these important connections, including studies on visceral fat inflammation and insulin resistance (PMID: 30549014, 35953124), a six-month randomized trial examining sugary beverages and visceral fat accumulation (PMID: 22205311), a systematic review of 84 randomized controlled trials investigating exercise and visceral fat reduction (PMID: 38031812), and research demonstrating the benefits of resistance training for reducing visceral fat (PMID: 34536199). 

Remember, reducing visceral fat is about much more than looking slimmer—it's about improving your metabolic health, reducing excess inflammatory activity, and protecting your body from the inside out. Small, consistent changes can lead to meaningful improvements over time. Wishing you good health and continued healing. Dr. Mandell

videos.summary_source_text:
Hellebuyck Won't Play in Winnipeg ft. Keith Kavanaugh | The Sheet with Jeff Marek & Greg Wyshynski Connor Hellebuyck's highly anticipated return to Winnipeg will have to wait, and the New Jersey Devils have sparked a major controversy with their decision to keep him out of Tuesday's game against the Jets.

Jeff Marek and Greg Wyshynski break down the statement released by Devils GM Sunny Mehta following New Jersey's shutout victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs, the reasoning behind the decision, and why Hellebuyck was adamant about facing his former team.

Did the Devils make the right call? Why release such a detailed public statement? And do Winnipeg Jets fans deserve the chance to welcome Hellebuyck back after his messy departure from the organization?

Keith Kavanagh of PuckPedia joins the show to offer additional perspective from the Devils' side, provide context surrounding the decision, and help unpack one of the NHL's biggest stories.

Elsewhere, the guys recap a busy Hockey Hall of Fame weekend, including Brady Tkachuk dropping the gloves with Nikita Zadorov, the Chicago Blackhawks' continued struggles and commitment to Jeff Blashill, Cutter Gauthier's latest hat trick against the Pittsburgh Penguins, the Calgary Flames picking up a win, and much more from around the NHL.

She also discusses the Rockies' longstanding culture of loyalty and why looking outside the organization for new perspectives could help move the franchise forward.

videos.title: GPT-6 Cyber: OpenAI's New AI Found 81 Hidden Firefox Security Flaws
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-6 Cyber: OpenAI's New AI Found 81 Hidden Firefox Security Flaws Try Unlimited Seedance 2.5 on OpenArt: https://openart.ai/home?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=influencer&utm_campaign=infl-youtube--na-acq-web&ref=BitBiasedAI-sd25

OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber reportedly generated **948 working Linux kernel exploits in just ten days**, discovered 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities, and scored 48.5% on ExploitGym. The estimated cost? Around **$1,280 per working exploit**.

Those numbers suggest a major shift in AI-powered cybersecurity. But there's a catch: the headline benchmarks, the actual capabilities, and what independent researchers can verify tell three different stories.

OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber on November 5 as a specialized cybersecurity variant of GPT-6 Astra, designed to discover vulnerabilities, reproduce security flaws, develop working exploits, and help researchers test defenses. Unlike ordinary ChatGPT models, GPT-6 Cyber is restricted to vetted customers through OpenAI's Daybreak Red program, with identity verification, hardware security keys, and additional access controls.

The Linux experiment is particularly revealing. According to OpenAI, a multi-agent pipeline scanned approximately 5,000 security-relevant locations in the Linux kernel, identified 2,308 candidate crashes, confirmed 1,724 bugs, and produced 948 working exploits. OpenAI reports that 588 of those exploits targeted previously unknown vulnerabilities.

The entire experiment reportedly consumed $1,213,430 in API credits. Compared with traditional vulnerability research and exploit-development costs, that raises an uncomfortable question: **What happens when discovering serious software vulnerabilities becomes dramatically cheaper than fixing them?**

Then there's Firefox.

OpenAI says GPT-6 Cyber identified 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities and supplied reproducible evidence to Mozilla. Firefox 159's security advisory provides evidence of substantial security fixes, but the public record doesn't independently connect all 81 reported discoveries to GPT-6 Cyber.

The comparison with Anthropic is also important. Mozilla previously reported protections for 271 vulnerabilities discovered with Anthropic's Mythos Preview. Different testing conditions and counting methods make direct comparisons difficult, but the broader trend is unmistakable: AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is creating an enormous new workload for software maintainers.

And the benchmark story gets even more interesting.

However, the general-purpose GPT-6 Astra reportedly achieved 42.4% without the same cyber specialization. That makes the additional improvement from cyber-specific training considerably smaller than the headline comparison suggests.

Google's Gemini 4 Carbon is another serious competitor, with an independently unverified leaderboard listing it at 53.5% on ExploitGym. Meanwhile, OpenAI's general-purpose model with safeguards enabled scored zero on certain exploit tasks because it refused to perform them. That's an important distinction between lacking technical capability and being restricted from using it.

OpenAI has also classified GPT-6 Cyber as **Critical** under its cybersecurity Preparedness Framework. Its reported honeypot evaluations show a dramatic reduction in unauthorized, out-of-scope actions compared with GPT-5.6 Cyber. But even a small failure rate becomes significant when automated systems operate at scale.

We also examine OpenAI's reported Dragos power-grid security experiment, the $1 billion Daybreak initiative, and the growing competition between OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic to develop powerful cybersecurity AI while restricting potentially dangerous capabilities.

The bigger question isn't simply whether GPT-6 Cyber is better at hacking.

It's whether defenders can patch vulnerabilities quickly enough when AI systems can discover them at unprecedented scale, and what happens when similar capabilities become available outside tightly controlled programs.

This breakdown separates OpenAI's reported results from independently verifiable evidence, examines the limitations behind the benchmarks, and explores what GPT-6 Cyber could mean for cybersecurity researchers, open-source maintainers, businesses, and the future of AI-powered security.

videos.title: The ONLY 2 DB Biceps Exercises You Need (NO, SERIOUSLY!)
videos.summary_source_text:
The ONLY 2 DB Biceps Exercises You Need (NO, SERIOUSLY!) Get big biceps here - https://athleanx.com
Subscribe to the ATHLEAN-X channel here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMW

What if I told you that here were only 2 dumbbell biceps exercises you need to grow bigger biceps, would you believe me? In this video, I am going to show you how only two dumbbell biceps exercises are all that is required to build big biceps. Remember, it comes down to not only the choice of the exercise you make, but how do them that makes all the difference.

The first exercise out of the only 2 dumbbell biceps exercises you need to build bigger biceps is a variation of an already popular biceps exercise. You might have seen or you are already doing the incline curl, but there is a better way to do it that will help you to build bigger biceps. Instead of performing the standard incline curl, I want you to do an incline drag curl to target the long head of the biceps.

This exercise combines the benefits of the incline curl and the drag curl while keeping the limitations of the incline curl out of the equation. It starts, however, with the incline position of the bench. You want to aim for about 60 degrees as too far upright will eliminate the stretch you get on the biceps at the bottom of the range of motion. A lesser incline, say 45-30 degrees, will allow you to get a stretch on the biceps, but to a degree that will likely cause discomfort on the biceps tendon and the anterior shoulder structure.

You are going to want to use light weight when performing this dumbbell biceps exercise as it will be all you can really handle. The key here is to eliminate the momentum you might be using on the incline curl and eliminate over activation of the front delt as you swing the dumbbells in order to move the weight. Shoulder flexion does come into play, but a little later in the range of motion of the incline drag curl. So, keep your elbows in place as you curl the weight up, essentially dragging the dumbbell straight up as you curl. At the top of the range of motion, you are going to want to supinate the dumbbells as much as you can while you get a small amount of shoulder flexion as we know to get bigger biceps, you want to activate all 3 functions of the biceps to get a complete contraction of the biceps muscles: elbow flexion, supination, and shoulder flexion.

The second exercise of the only 2 dumbbell bicep exercises you need is one you are probably already doing, but, there is a possibility you are doing it wrong. First, it's important to note why the dumbbell preacher curl is the perfect compliment to the incline drag curl we already discussed. If the drag curl is targeting the long head of the biceps, especially on stretch, then we need to next try to influence the biceps short head and peak contraction. The other great part is that this preacher curl can be done with the exact same setup as the incline drag curl.

The preacher curl is immensely popular, but there is a right way and a wrong way of performing the exercise that will either prevent or lead to a biceps tendon tear. If you keep the same bench setup as the incline curl, you are already headed in the right direction. You see, too steep of an incline on the bench or preacher pad and not standing over it is going to lead to a lot of stress on the biceps tendon.

Instead, when you perform the preacher curl, you want to stand over the incline of the bench where your triceps stay flush with the bench at all times win the range of motion. This will allow you to use your lats to assist in the movement and protect your biceps in the process. As you curl the dumbbell, you want to dig your elbow and triceps into the bench, almost trying to pull it towards yourself as you curl. This will take the biceps out of a vulnerable position and allow you to curl the weight without risk.

With your arm more out in front of you, you are already getting the necessary shoulder flexion that influences the biceps contraction. On top of that, the elbow flexion (curl) and forced supination will lead to greater biceps growth.

With those two dumbbell biceps exercises, you are training the biceps through stretch and peak contraction - covering the whole range of motion of the biceps in order to build bigger biceps.

Topped shots and inconsistent contact from one day to the next usually come from standing up or lifting during the golf swing, and it's what Eric Cogorno sees every day in golf lessons with regular golfers. When your shoulders turn too level, your body moves farther from the ground, and constantly getting farther from and closer to the ground is the least consistent way to play. The fix is shoulder tilt: your left shoulder goes down and in and under your chin in the backswing, about 40°, and your right shoulder goes down with even more tilt, about 55°, in the golf downswing, the same pattern you see in Tommy Fleetwood's golf swing. These golf swing tips and a simple golf drill with a second ball about one yard outside the first show you how much tilt to feel, so you can build a consistent golf swing and learn how to hit irons solid. If you leave this video without trying this golf drill, you're leaving solid, consistent contact on the table.

What You'll Learn:
• Why standing up in your golf swing leads to topped shots
• How to move your left shoulder down and under your chin
• What the Tommy Fleetwood swing shows about left shoulder tilt

videos.title: New 217mph Audi Nuvolari made me SICK!
videos.summary_source_text:
New 217mph Audi Nuvolari made me SICK! Is the Audi Nuvolari the ultimate hybrid supercar?!

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-09-11

Mat’s got his hands on the Audi Nuvolari! 

He’s flown over to Spain, and he’s going to have a chance to walk around a pre-production model, take it out on the road, and push it to its limits on track! 

The question is, with it being such a departure from Audi’s recent design language, is it really worth the eye-waveringly large price tag? It’s time to find out, starting with the design… 

One thing’s for sure: there’s no denying the Audi Nuvolari stands out compared to any Audi released in the past several years! The entire bodywork is made of carbon fibre, and it really stands out on the road. Up top you’ll find two huge vents flanking the rectangular grille, all of which are made out of aluminium - there’s no plastic to be found here! There’s a huge vent in the bonnet to help with airflow, and around the side you’ll find side blades which are a nod to those found on the R8. Around the back you’ll find a huge carbon fibre diffuser, and when you look under the car you’ll note multiple different fins to help distribute airflow. 

The interior of the car may have a simple layout, but it’s all incredibly well built. There’s almost no plastic to be found throughout the cabin, with leather, metal and Alcantara-like material found everywhere. There’s a large rectangular display on the centre console, and the steering wheel is covered to control a whole host of functions. Anyone looking for some storage may be out of luck, though - there are no door bins, and not even a cupholder! But then again, what would you expect in a supercar like this? 

As for the performance, the Nuvolari is equipped with the same 4-litre twin-turbo V8 as found in the Lamborghini Temerario. This alone produces 800hp and 730Nm, which is sent to the rear wheels only. However, there are dual motors on the front axle, where these and the engine combine to produce 1,001hp! This makes it the most powerful Audi ever produced! 

But of course, a car such as this doesn’t come cheap, costing £526,990! It’s limited to 499 units, with only 25 coming to the UK - and they’re all sold out! But do you think this is the greatest Audi ever produced? Let us know in the comments! Is the Audi Nuvolari the ultimate hybrid supercar?!

videos.summary_source_text:
Every Shot of Jon Rahm’s Winning Back Nine | 2026 Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship Watch the Back Nine on Sunday, presented by Nexo, as Jon Rahm claims his sixth Rolex Series title and 11th DP World Tour victory at the 2026 Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After 40 events, five global swings, the Back 9 and four Majors, the DP World Tour Play-Offs are upon us. The top 70 available players from the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World tee it up this week at Yas Links before the top 50 then move on to the season-finale at the DP World Tour Championship. Both those events form part of the Rolex Series, with Patrick Reed, Tom Kim and JJ Spaun having already been crowned Rolex Series champions in 2026. With full playing privileges on the DP World Tour now secured the focus turns to the quest to be Europe’s Number One and claim the Harry Vardon Trophy. Rory McIlroy is looking to equal Colin Montgomerie's record of eight season-long wins with his fifth in a row but the Northern Irishman is in the unusual position of being the hunter rather than the hunted. Last year, Aaron Rai beat fellow Englishman Tommy Fleetwood in a play-off to win his second Rolex Series title at Yas Links, five years on from his first at the Scottish Open. The 70 player field is stacked with star-studded names, featuring 6 major winners including Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm and Patrick Reed alongside three-time season winner Eugenio Chacarra who will be hoping to add a Rolex Series title to his CV. With enhanced points on offer it also means that the jostling for dual membership with the PGA Tour is far from over.

Every week you can find extended tournament highlights and individual player highlights from the likes of Rory McIlroy, Justin Rose and Tommy Fleetwood. videos.title: PGA Tour Highlights | Round 4 | World Wide Technology | 2026
videos.summary_source_text:
PGA Tour Highlights | Round 4 | World Wide Technology | 2026 Check out the best shots of the day from Round 4 of the 2026 World Wide Technology Championship, featuring Blades Brown, Ben James, Ryan Gerard, Chris Kirk, and Denny McCarthy, among others.

The World Wide Technology Championship returns to El Cardonal at Diamante as the FedExCup Fall enters its final stretch, with defending champion Ben Griffin looking to become the first back-to-back winner since Viktor Hovland. Ryan Gerard headlines the field as its highest-ranked player, while Griffin arrives off a T4 in Mexico. With just three events left in the season, players around the top-100 bubble, including Tony Finau and Lucas Glover are under pressure to secure their PGA Tour status. Young talents Jackson Koivun, Ben James and Blades Brown also tee it up, alongside European Ryder Cup captain Luke Donald.

videos.title: The Foods You Eat Could Be Feeding Cancer Cells | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
The Foods You Eat Could Be Feeding Cancer Cells | Dr. Mandell Are the foods you eat feeding cancer cells? Dr. Alan Mandell explains what happens when your body breaks down glucose, why cutting out sugar does not selectively starve a tumor, and what research says about everyday food choices and cancer risk. Learn about processed meats, alcohol and acetaldehyde, sugary drinks, fiber, whole grains, and the connection between diet and colorectal cancer risk. Get practical food swaps you can use without fear or false promises. No single food can cure or prevent cancer; this video explains how regular eating patterns can influence health and risk over time. For education only; discuss personal cancer concerns with your healthcare professional. 

PubMed research information:

Aune D, et al. “Dietary fibre, whole grains, and risk of colorectal cancer: systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of prospective studies.” BMJ. 2011;343:d6617. PMID: 22074852. The review found higher fiber, cereal fiber, and whole-grain intake was associated with lower colorectal cancer risk. 

Chan DSM, et al. “Red and processed meat and colorectal cancer incidence: meta-analysis of prospective studies.” PLoS One. 2011;6(6):e20456. PMID: 21674008. The meta-analysis found processed-meat intake was associated with increased colorectal cancer risk. 

Rumgay H, et al. “Alcohol and Cancer: Epidemiology and Biological Mechanisms.” Nutrients. 2021;13(9):3173. PMID: 34579050. This review describes evidence linking alcohol with several cancers and discusses acetaldehyde-related DNA damage.

videos.summary_source_text:
Round 4 Highlights | 2026 Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship Highlights of the final round of the 2026 Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, where Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton and Francesco Laporta battled for the title in Abu Dhabi. 

► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

After 40 events, five global swings, the Back 9 and four Majors, the DP World Tour Play-Offs are upon us. The top 70 available players from the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World tee it up this week at Yas Links before the top 50 then move on to the season-finale at the DP World Tour Championship. Both those events form part of the Rolex Series, with Patrick Reed, Tom Kim and JJ Spaun having already been crowned Rolex Series champions in 2026. With full playing privileges on the DP World Tour now secured the focus turns to the quest to be Europe’s Number One and claim the Harry Vardon Trophy. videos.title: Dizzy When You Stand Up? What It Means After 40
videos.summary_source_text:
Dizzy When You Stand Up? What It Means After 40 Does the room go grey for a moment when you get up? In the first ten seconds after you stand, up to a litre of blood shifts towards your legs, and your body has to catch it. This video explains what is happening, why it gets more common after 40, and how to check it at home: a simple 10-second self-check, then the lying-and-standing blood pressure routine doctors use. You'll also get seven practical steps and the warning signs that mean you should see a doctor.

Chapters

0:28 Why it matters after 40
1:04 Ten seconds, slowed down
3:13 Three myths
4:26 Seven steps, including the home check
7:41 When to see a doctor
8:32 Bringing it together

Stop Doing These 5 Things Before Bed—Your Body Needs Better Sleep!  Dr. Mandell Are you sleeping 7 or 8 hours and still waking up feeling tired, exhausted, or completely drained? The problem may not be how long you're sleeping, but what you're doing before bedtime! In this powerful health video, Dr. Alan Mandell, Motivationaldoc, reveals five common nighttime habits that can interfere with your natural sleep cycle, disrupt important hormones, overstimulate your nervous system, and prevent your body from getting the restorative sleep it needs. Discover how bright lights and nighttime screen exposure affect melatonin production, how eating heavy meals before bed can interfere with digestion and trigger acid reflux, and how caffeine blocks adenosine, the natural chemical that builds sleep pressure in your brain. You'll also learn how late-night vigorous exercise can affect body temperature and alertness, and why taking your worries, stress, and racing thoughts into bed can make falling asleep so difficult. Dr. Mandell explains the fascinating connection between your brain, circadian rhythm, cortisol, sympathetic nervous system, and your body's natural ability to rest and recover. Most importantly, you'll discover simple, practical changes you can begin making tonight to support deeper, more consistent, and more refreshing sleep. Quality sleep is essential for memory, immune function, emotional well-being, cardiovascular health, and the body's natural recovery processes. I det här avsnittet av Bilpodden Varför? Därför! sitter Felix och jag i nya i3 på slingriga vägar utanför Marseille. Vi pratar om varför 3-serien är så central för BMW och om gamla lilla i3:an, citybilen i kolfiber som fortfarande ser modern ut. Och om hur BMW kan bygga en elbil och en bensinbil som ser likadana ut men inte delar en enda karosspanel.

Vi går igenom 40:an mot 50:an, cylindriska battericeller, 400 kW laddning och Heart of Joy, datorn som ska stå för körglädjen. Sen kör vi. Hur känns styrningen? Bromsarna? videos.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Google's New AI Video Model Is INSANE
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Google's New AI Video Model Is INSANE Try Unlimited Seedance 2.5 on OpenArt: https://openart.ai/home?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=influencer&utm_campaign=infl-youtube--na-acq-web&ref=BitBiasedAI-sd25

Google just launched Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, an AI video model that can generate a 15-second video with sound for about $1.05. It's 30% cheaper than Omni 1.1, supports conversational video editing, and promises more accurate text, better camera control, and improved character consistency.

But there's a catch. An independent tester called it the most instruction-exact AI video model he'd used, while also reporting that roughly one in four instructions gets skipped.

So how good is Google's new AI video generator when you move beyond carefully selected demos?

Google announced Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash on November 5, bringing its video generation technology into general availability through the Gemini API and Google Cloud. The model supports clips from 3 to 15 seconds, generation at 360p and 720p, and upscaling to 1080p or 4K.

At just $0.07 per second for 720p generation, Google's pricing makes AI video experimentation significantly more affordable. But the cost of generating a clip isn't necessarily the cost of producing a finished video.

Google says Omni 1.2 Flash can edit existing videos through natural-language instructions. Want to change a sunset into a nighttime scene? Replace an object without changing the background? Add rain while preserving the original camera movement? That's the promise behind conversational AI video editing.

The model also supports image references, motion references, first-and-last-frame guidance, synchronized dialogue, lip-sync, and more controlled cinematic camera movements.

But how much of that actually works?

We examine Google's official demonstrations, including a continuous drone-style flight through the Pantheon, a dramatic shoreline zoom-out, an octopus-to-dancer transformation, animated science explainers with readable labels, and multi-character dialogue.

Then we put Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash through increasingly difficult video generation challenges.

We start with a cinematic forest scene featuring two deer, realistic lighting, smooth camera movement, and generated audio. Next comes a science explainer testing whether the model can correctly spell and position labels like Sunlight, Refraction, and Rainbow.

From there, we explore conversational editing with a red sports car, transforming a desert sunset into a nighttime scene before adding heavy rain and reflections.

We also test character consistency using reference images, checking whether the same adventurer maintains her facial features, clothing, and appearance across separate video generations.

Finally, we push into complex physics and multi-step instructions: falling dominoes, moving objects, synchronized dancers, and a dramatic astronaut-to-alien-temple camera movement.

These challenges target some of the exact weaknesses Google acknowledges, including fast action, complex physics, and rapid scene changes.

Independent testing by Rohit Rao at Segmind adds another perspective. Across 20 launch-day tests costing $16.17, he praised the model's instruction accuracy while identifying problems with skipped instructions, floaty human motion, counting, and numerical chart accuracy.

And the competition matters.

Seedance 2.0 and Kling 3 remain important alternatives. According to Rao's assessment, Seedance 2.0 still performs better for photorealistic people, cinematic footage, and physics-heavy action, while Omni 1.2 Flash shows particular promise for typography, explainers, chart animations, and precise edits.

We also examine the real economics of AI video generation. A single 15-second clip costs approximately $1.05 at 720p, but retries, corrections, editing passes, and upscaling can make the final production considerably more expensive.

So is Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash a breakthrough for AI video creation, or a specialized tool that excels at following certain instructions while struggling with cinematic realism?

And should creators, marketers, developers, and businesses choose Google's model over Seedance and Kling?

Watch the full comparison to see where Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash delivers, where it struggles, and what Google's approach means for the future of AI video generation.

These challenges target some of the exact weaknesses Google acknowledges, including fast action, complex physics, and rapid scene changes.

Independent testing by Rohit Rao at Segmind adds another perspective. Across 20 launch-day tests costing $16.17, he praised the model's instruction accuracy while identifying problems with skipped instructions, floaty human motion, counting, and numerical chart accuracy.

And the competition matters.

Seedance 2.0 and Kling 3 remain important alternatives. According to Rao's assessment, Seedance 2.0 still performs better for photorealistic people, cinematic footage, and physics-heavy action, while Omni 1.2 Flash shows particular promise for typography, explainers, chart animations, and precise edits.

We also examine the real economics of AI video generation. A single 15-second clip costs approximately $1.05 at 720p, but retries, corrections, editing passes, and upscaling can make the final production considerably more expensive.

So is Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash a breakthrough for AI video creation, or a specialized tool that excels at following certain instructions while struggling with cinematic realism?

And should creators, marketers, developers, and businesses choose Google's model over Seedance and Kling?

Watch the full comparison to see where Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash delivers, where it struggles, and what Google's approach means for the future of AI video generation.

After 40 events, five global swings, the Back 9 and four Majors, the DP World Tour Play-Offs are upon us. GPT-7 Is Coming: OpenAI 10 Trillion Parameter Secret AI Model! Try Unlimited Seedance 2.5 on OpenArt: https://openart.ai/home?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=influencer&utm_campaign=infl-youtube--na-acq-web&ref=BitBiasedAI-sd25

GPT-7 leaks are everywhere. A rumored 10-trillion-parameter model, mysterious benchmark screenshots, claims of autonomous AI agents running for days, and predictions that OpenAI's next model could finally achieve AGI. But almost none of those supposed GPT-7 specifications have been verified.

Here's what makes this story different: OpenAI has reported testing an internal model significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra. According to the company, roughly 10,000 model instances worked for 88 hours on a claimed solution to the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize problem. The model reportedly remains in training.

So does GPT-7 already exist? When will it launch? And could it fundamentally change how AI works?

The answer is more complicated than the leaks suggest.

OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra arrived in September 2026 with reported scores of 97.6% on FrontierMath Tier 4 and 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3 under OpenAI's testing conditions. It also became the company's first model classified as "critical" under its Preparedness Framework because of advanced cybersecurity capabilities.

Then OpenAI reportedly canceled GPT-6.1 Astra just before DevDay. The reason wasn't a lack of intelligence. The upgrade failed important safety and reliability tests involving authorization, scope, and accurately reporting its own actions.

That raises a much bigger question: What happens when AI becomes more capable than humans can reliably supervise?

We investigate OpenAI's published research, including mathematical proofs, Lean 4 verification, the controversial Navier–Stokes claim, and the enormous computing resources behind long-running AI research agents.

We also examine the rumored GPT-7 codename "Bel," claims of more than 10 trillion parameters, alleged benchmark leaks, and predictions of a 2027 release. Which details have credible evidence, and which trace back to anonymous social media posts?

And there's another twist: GPT-7 might not even be called GPT-7.

OpenAI has already demonstrated that major capability improvements don't always require a new model number. GPT-5.6, GPT-6 Astra, and GPT-6.1 Sol reveal a changing strategy around intelligence, pricing, efficiency, and deployment.

Meanwhile, the competition isn't standing still.

Google's Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 4 Carbon, Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5, xAI's Grok 4.7, and DeepSeek's increasingly efficient models are all putting pressure on OpenAI. The next generation won't be judged on benchmarks alone. Cost, reliability, autonomous execution, and real-world usefulness could matter just as much.

We also examine whether AI agents can realistically operate for days without human intervention, conduct independent research, write complex software, or eventually contribute to developing their own successors.

Could GPT-7 help build GPT-8? Could it qualify as artificial general intelligence? And which professions would experience the consequences first?

Software engineering, financial analysis, scientific research, and knowledge work are already showing signs of change. But there's a major difference between AI assisting with a task and AI reliably completing it without supervision.

The most important breakthrough might not be a larger parameter count or another record-breaking benchmark. It could be an AI system that stays within its permissions, accurately reports its actions, and completes complex work reliably over extended periods.

The next OpenAI model could be extraordinary. But until its capabilities are independently tested, the difference between confirmed research and speculation matters more than ever.

Watch the full breakdown before believing another GPT-7 leak.

videos.title: We Put Rory McIlroy On A Boat...Then Kept Moving It Further Away
videos.summary_source_text:
We Put Rory McIlroy On A Boat...Then Kept Moving It Further Away Can Rory McIlroy hit the iconic 18th green at Yas Links from a moving boat?

Ahead of the 2026 Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, staged by the Abu Dhabi Sports Council and the DP World Tour, six-time Major Champion Rory McIlroy took on one of the most unique challenges of his career on the waters surrounding Yas Links Abu Dhabi.

Known for producing long drives on dry-land, the reigning Masters Champion and Race to Dubai winner swapped the stability of the fairway for a specially constructed platform built on top of a moving boat, with one target in mind: the green of the famous par-five 18th hole at Yas Links.

The challenge began at 150 yards, but with every successful attempt the boat moved further away. McIlroy was then tasked with finding the green from 225 yards before taking on the ultimate test, launching full drives from approximately 325 yards across the water towards one of golf's most recognisable finishing holes.

Did he manage to complete all three levels?

videos.title: Mucus Stuck in Your Throat? Why It Happens After 40
videos.summary_source_text:
Mucus Stuck in Your Throat? Why It Happens After 40 That mucus stuck at the back of your throat often isn't a sign you're making too much. More often, it isn't moving. After 40, the tiny hairs (cilia) that sweep mucus out of your airways beat more slowly. Dry mouth from medicines, silent reflux and some blood pressure pills can make it worse. This video explains how your throat's cleaning system works, clears up three common myths (milk, green mucus and throat clearing), and gives you 7 simple, low-cost steps to try this week. It also covers the signs that mean you should see a doctor.

videos.title: Possibly The EASIEST WayTo Hit Driver Straight
videos.summary_source_text:
Possibly The EASIEST WayTo Hit Driver Straight Struggle with slicing your driver, losing distance or feeling like you have to work too hard to create speed?

In this Danny Maude golf lesson, you’ll learn a counterintuitive driver drill that can help you square the clubface, reduce your slice and create more clubhead speed without trying to hit the golf ball harder.

The surprising part is that the drill starts by doing something most golfers would think is completely wrong:

**Opening the clubface at address.**

Danny Maude discovered this while working with a student who was slicing his driver badly. Within just a few swings, the slice began to change into a draw, the ball started finding the fairway more consistently and he appeared to gain extra distance — even though distance was never the goal.

In this golf lesson you’ll learn:

• Why trying to close the clubface can sometimes make a slice worse  
• How an open clubface drill can teach you to square the face naturally  
• Why exaggeration drills can change your golf swing faster  
• How to stop cutting across the golf ball  
• Why golfers often lunge their body towards the target  
• How the hands and arms create clubhead speed  
• Why trying to power the swing with the body can reduce distance  
• A simple feet-together drill for more speed and better balance  
• How to use the sound of the club to create more clubhead speed  
• How to train a freer release through impact  
• Why the body should support the arms rather than dominate the swing  

The key idea is simple.

Rather than telling your wrists, arms and body exactly how to move, create a task that encourages the movement you want.

For a slicer, deliberately opening the clubface gives your body a reason to learn how to square it through impact. That can help the hands and arms become more active, reduce the need to lunge with the body and create a much freer release of the golf club.

Practice Plan: https://www.dannymaude.com/change-this-to-hit-driver-straight

07:50 How to practise the open-face drill

videos.summary_source_text:
World's greatest engine: DRAG RACE Is BMW’s B58 engine the greatest engine of all time? 

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-07-11

It’s time for a B58 head-to-head! 

While all four cars in this line-up may seem vastly different to each other, they have one thing in common - under each of their bonnets is a BMW B58 engine! 

This 3-litre straight-six turbo may be one of the most famous engines around, but how does it fare when used across four different cars? It’s time to find out! 

First up we have the Morgan Supersport 400. Here the B58 produces 408hp and 500Nm, with this power sent to the rear wheels only via an 8-speed automatic gearbox. It’s by far the lightest car here, at just 1,170kg, but it’s also easily the most expensive, costing a colossal £138,883! 

Alongside it we have the BMW M240i. This B58 produces 392hp and 540Nm, but unlike the Morgan, this power is sent to all four wheels! It tips the scales at 1,690kg, and it costs around £50,000. 

Up next we have the Mk5 Supra. Here the B58 has been limited to just 340hp and 500Nm, and this is sent to the rear wheels only via an 8-speed auto. It weighs in at 1,495kg, and it costs £53,000 - or at least it did when last on sale in 2023. 

Finally we come to the INEOS Grenadier. Once again it’s powered by a B58, and it would usually produces 286hp and 450Nm. However, it’s been tuned, so it now puts down 460hp and 650Nm! Along with the tune it’s also been lightened, so the weight has dropped from 2,665kg to 2,480kg. The starting price of a regular INEOS is around £72,000. 

So how will this one play out - will the BMW’s AWD propel it to victory? Or will the super-light Morgan snatch it? There’s only one way to find out for sure - LET’S RACE!

1600hp M140i v Lambo Revuelto: https://bit.ly/Carwow-Drag-Race-0411

It’s time for a B58 head-to-head! 

While all four cars in this line-up may seem vastly different to each other, they have one thing in common - under each of their bonnets is a BMW B58 engine! 

This 3-litre straight-six turbo may be one of the most famous engines around, but how does it fare when used across four different cars? It’s time to find out! 

First up we have the Morgan Supersport 400. Here the B58 produces 408hp and 500Nm, with this power sent to the rear wheels only via an 8-speed automatic gearbox. It’s by far the lightest car here, at just 1,170kg, but it’s also easily the most expensive, costing a colossal £138,883! 

Alongside it we have the BMW M240i. This B58 produces 392hp and 540Nm, but unlike the Morgan, this power is sent to all four wheels! It tips the scales at 1,690kg, and it costs around £50,000. 

Up next we have the Mk5 Supra. Here the B58 has been limited to just 340hp and 500Nm, and this is sent to the rear wheels only via an 8-speed auto. It weighs in at 1,495kg, and it costs £53,000 - or at least it did when last on sale in 2023. 

Finally we come to the INEOS Grenadier. Once again it’s powered by a B58, and it would usually produces 286hp and 450Nm. However, it’s been tuned, so it now puts down 460hp and 650Nm! Along with the tune it’s also been lightened, so the weight has dropped from 2,665kg to 2,480kg. The starting price of a regular INEOS is around £72,000. 

So how will this one play out - will the BMW’s AWD propel it to victory? Or will the super-light Morgan snatch it? There’s only one way to find out for sure - LET’S RACE!

videos.summary_source_text:
06.11.26 - RIFT Training RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

What Are Electrolytes? The Mineral Your Body Can't Live Without Electrolytes are electrically charged minerals that help your body conduct nerve impulses, contract and relax muscles, regulate pH, and maintain fluid balance. Potassium is one of the most important electrolytes because it supports so many essential functions, from digestion and circulation to energy and heart rhythm.

Watch the FULL video here: https://youtu.be/1hXpb3T96PU

When potassium is low, you can experience:
• Swollen ankles and fluid retention
• Fatigue and reduced exercise endurance
• Muscle cramps, twitching, and tremors
• Irregular heart rhythms
• Constipation
• Difficulty sleeping

Potassium also plays an important role in stomach acid balance, protein digestion, and calcium regulation. Getting enough potassium helps your muscles, nerves, and digestive system function properly while supporting healthy blood pressure and circulation.

videos.title: Just ¼ Teaspoon Every Night to Help Reduce Inflammation Throughout Your Body!  Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Just ¼ Teaspoon Every Night to Help Reduce Inflammation Throughout Your Body!  Dr. Mandell Did you know that one simple golden spice sitting in your kitchen contains a powerful natural compound that researchers have been studying for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties? In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell reveals how turmeric and its active compound, curcumin, can support your body's natural defenses against oxidative stress, promote a healthier digestive system, and contribute to overall wellness. Inflammation plays an important role in your immune system, but when it becomes chronic, it can affect many different areas of your health. Discover the fascinating connection between your gut and your brain, how the trillions of microorganisms living inside your digestive tract influence digestion and immune function, and why maintaining a balanced gut microbiome is so important. You'll also learn how turmeric interacts with the digestive system, how bile supports the breakdown and absorption of fats, and why researchers are interested in curcumin's potential effects on intestinal inflammation and gut health. We'll discuss the importance of proper nutrition, regular bowel movements, healthy gut bacteria, and the foods that nourish your digestive tract. You'll also discover why combining turmeric with foods containing healthy fats can improve the absorption of curcumin, and how black pepper contains piperine, a compound that can increase curcumin absorption. Whether you're looking to support your digestive health, maintain a healthier gut, or learn more about the connection between inflammation and overall wellness, this video shares valuable information about a remarkable spice that has been used in traditional cooking for centuries. A quarter teaspoon of culinary turmeric can be an easy way to incorporate this spice into your meals, although that specific nightly amount has not been clinically established to reduce inflammation throughout the body. Remember, taking care of your gut is an important part of taking care of your overall health. Please share this video with your friends and family, subscribe for more natural health education, and most importantly, make it a great day! Dr. Alan Mandell, DC — Motivationaldoc.

Research References (PubMed):

Hewlings SJ, Kalman DS. Curcumin: A Review of Its Effects on Human Health. Foods. 2017. Reviews curcumin's anti-inflammatory and antioxidant mechanisms.

Shoba G, et al. Influence of Piperine on the Pharmacokinetics of Curcumin in Animals and Human Volunteers. Planta Medica. 1998. Examines increased curcumin bioavailability when combined with piperine.

Scazzocchio B, et al. Interaction between Gut Microbiota and Curcumin: A New Key of Understanding for the Health Effects of Curcumin. Nutrients. 2020. Explores the relationship between curcumin and the gut microbiome.

Educational Disclaimer: This video is for educational purposes only and is not intended to diagnose, treat, or cure any disease. Turmeric used as a food spice is different from concentrated curcumin supplements, which can interact with medications and are not appropriate for everyone.

***********************************

videos.channel: Easier & Better golf with your guide Marcus Edblad
videos.summary_source_text:
Understand weight shift and club path… If we force weight shift we lose the natural ability we learned and golf will not be pretty. Let your weight follow the club and it will start working again.

golfswing #golf #golftips 

Online lesson are now a possibility on Skillest: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

0:00 Intro - Learn the curve before we change the swing path
1:00 It is good to start with a hook

Let me help you get an effortless golfswing with speed, distance and accuracy. I call it the circle of speed. A good release will help you to a better impact and longer drives and irons without slice and hook. How to swing a golf club need to be adjusted to your skill level and experience. 

Long and straight is the goal for everyone but it takes time. Try to focus on one thing not everything when you practise. Impact, face control and swingpath will always be the most important part to drill. We focus too much on rotation but no good golf shot will be executed just by rotating. 

We also need to understand that many myths in golf are missleading. Everything that you find on the internet isn’t true. Ben Hogan, Sam Snead are two of the legends that are often misunderstood.  To understand golf we need to take it step by step and learn every part of the swing before we move on to the next. It's like a big jigsaw puzzle that we all can figure out. 

I will never call a slice sexy but a high draw is beautiful in a very special way. Some pro's that hit draw: Rory McIroy, Xander Schauffele, Patrick Reed, Sepp Straka, Bryson Dechambeau  and many, many more. 

We shall not keep our head still, only start with the hips, look only at the ball or keep the left or right arm straight. Understand what do do with the club and let your body find the best way possible. 

This is not Rick Shiels, Saguto golf, Danny Maude, Meandmygolf, the Average Golfer, Malaska, Mark Crossfield, Alex Elliot Golf or Paige Spiranac. This is a method that anyone can learn if you give it a chance. 

If you use callaway, ping, titleist, takomo or taylor made clubs doesn’t matter you can learn to hit good golf shots. Your loft or your shaft on the club will not change but you can always get better. 

Find what inspires you. Golf basics are the same for everyone. The pga tour, longdrivers or other good golfers can all help you find better golf shots. Watch what they do instead of listed to what they say. Listen mostly to your body and figure out what you need to do to produce the same results as the pros on TV. Be careful when you watch a golf swing in slow motion. The result isn't always what the golfer is trying to do. Feel and real are seldom the same. 

We can find inspiration in a lot of things. You can find training motivation watching movies like Rocky, Tin Cup or Happy Gilmore and find mental inspiration in legends like Arnold Schwarzenegger, Hulk Hogan, Sylvester Stallone or Mike Tyson. Maybe we sometimes need to hear about crazy achievements from people like David Goggins, Jocko Willink, Ct Fletcher, Jim Rohn or Tony Robbins. 

Mike Malaska, Mike Austin, Mike Dunaway, Pete Cowen and Steve Pratt are some of my favorite golf instructors online. Find the tips that make your golf better. Decide what you want to hit. I teach a draw but many like a fade and nobody likes a hook or slice. 

Your hips or your lag is not the key to golf. Your hands will decide the shot and you can do like Tiger Woods and trust your hands. Teach your hands to hit different shots. Hit big hooks and slices to understand what happens. Only straight is not gonna teach you anything. 

Bryson Dechambeu and Kyle Birkshire can inspire you to hit it longer. Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson can give you inspiration and motivation to test new things and new golf shots. Linn Grant, Viktor Hovland and Ludvig Aberg can show you the future of golf. 

The Masters, Players Championship, The Players, The Open and US Open can make you love golf even more. See the best in the world solve all the problems we all need to master any golf course. Golf is a craft and you need fantasy, feel and skills to master it.

Questions my videos will answer:

How to swing faster. How to hit longer. How to swing faster. How to hit your irons better. How to be better at anything. How to master the circle of speed. How to get a better short game. How to hit your wedge better. How to release the golf club. How to rotate in golf. Best tips for beginner golfers. How to hit down on the ball. How to hit up on the ball. How to rotate hips in the golf swing. How to hit straight every time. How to stop slicing. How to swing effortlessly.

videos.title: Elon Musk Is Building an AI Company With No Human Workers
videos.summary_source_text:
Elon Musk Is Building an AI Company With No Human Workers Try UNLIMITED SeeDance 2.5 on OpenArt: https://openart.ai/home?utm_source=yo...

Elon Musk promised to build an AI company with ZERO human employees. More than a year later, the biggest public progress update for xAI's Macrohard project is a claim that Digital Optimus can play halfway through Diablo. No public demo. No independent benchmark. No released product.

In August 2025, Musk announced Macrohard as a "purely AI software company" capable of challenging Microsoft by replacing entire teams with AI agents. Grok would coordinate hundreds of specialized agents handling coding, testing, design, and deployment. Musk even claimed the system could eventually "emulate the function of entire companies."

But by March 2026, the story had changed dramatically.

Business Insider reported that Macrohard had stalled, engineers had been reassigned, leadership had departed, and a data operation involving approximately 600 contracted workers had been suspended. On that very same day, Musk announced that Macrohard was becoming a joint Tesla and xAI project under a new name: Digital Optimus.

And that's where things get interesting.

Digital Optimus isn't a humanoid robot. It's a proposed real-time AI computer operator that watches your screen, processes the last five seconds of visual information, and controls a mouse and keyboard. Tesla's AI4 chip, which Musk priced at approximately $650, would handle fast reactions while Grok performs deeper reasoning using xAI's Nvidia infrastructure.

Musk claims this combination could eventually turn parked Tesla vehicles into computers capable of performing office work.

But can an AI that watches five seconds of screen activity actually replace an entire software company?

On October 10, 2026, Musk claimed Digital Optimus could play roughly halfway through a Diablo campaign, showed promising Counter-Strike skills, and was training on League of Legends. Yet no gameplay footage, scores, reproducible benchmarks, or independent evaluations accompanied those claims.

And the promised six-month development window had already passed.

Meanwhile, Tesla's involvement raises another question. The company invested $2 billion into xAI, which was subsequently acquired by SpaceX. Tesla shareholders had already filed a lawsuit alleging Musk diverted AI resources and opportunities from Tesla toward xAI. Those allegations remain separate from any proven wrongdoing.

Then there's Grok Bot.

Unlike Macrohard, Grok Bot actually launched in beta in August 2026. It offers persistent AI teammates with cloud computers, browser automation, reusable workflows, and parallel task execution. But xAI hasn't publicly established that Grok Bot is Macrohard, and its launch doesn't demonstrate a fully autonomous software company.

The distinction matters.

OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google are already developing computer-operating agents. Musk's proposed advantage isn't simply that an AI can click buttons. It's the possibility of doing so faster and more cheaply using Tesla's specialized hardware.

That could be a meaningful engineering breakthrough. But operating software isn't the same as running a business. Product strategy, customer relationships, security, compliance, accountability, and long-term decision-making remain unresolved challenges.

We break down what Musk originally promised, why Macrohard reportedly stalled, how Digital Optimus is supposed to work, what xAI has actually shipped, and why the gap between an impressive AI agent and an autonomous company is much larger than it sounds.

Is Macrohard a genuine breakthrough waiting for its public debut, or another ambitious Elon Musk announcement still searching for proof?

videos.title: Poor Circulation in Legs: 7 Things to Do After 60
videos.summary_source_text:
Poor Circulation in Legs: 7 Things to Do After 60 Your calves ache halfway to the shops, so you stop at a window and the pain fades. In Germany it's called "shop-window disease". Often it's narrowed leg arteries (peripheral artery disease, P.A.D.), and one of the best-proven treatments is the walk itself. We explain how blood travels down your arteries and back up through the calf pump. We also clear up three myths, go through seven low-cost steps to start this week, and cover the signs that mean it's time to see a doctor.

Want to hit more solid iron shots and start hitting more greens in regulation? In this golf lesson, I'll break down three things great players do differently with their irons: consistently finding the center of the clubface, controlling their angle of attack, and playing a predictable shot shape. These fundamentals can help you improve distance control, accuracy, and overall ball striking without constantly changing your swing.

First, learn why centered contact matters so much and how even a small miss toward the toe or heel can affect distance and direction. You'll see a simple cardboard box and alignment stick drill that helps train your clubhead to return to the middle of the face. Next, I'll explain how angle of attack changes with each club, how ball position influences shaft lean, and why excessive grip pressure can prevent you from creating the proper impact conditions. You'll also learn practical drills using a tee, a towel behind the ball, and a line on the ground to improve low-point control and make cleaner contact.

Finally, discover why the best players don't constantly try to manufacture draws and fades. They understand their natural ball flight and choose targets that allow their typical shot shape to work toward the flag. If you want to hit your irons more consistently, improve your approach shots, and lower your scores, these three lessons are a great place to start.

One common cause of long COVID symptoms and chronic fatigue syndrome is impaired natural killer cell function. These immune cells are responsible for fighting viruses and destroying abnormal cells, including cancer cells. When they stop functioning properly, you could experience persistent exhaustion, chronic inflammation, and brain fog.

Anything that significantly increases cortisol can contribute to the reactivation of latent viruses, triggering post-viral fatigue and other symptoms.

Factors that contribute to viral reactivation include:
• Grief from a loss
• Poor sleep
• Elevated cortisol or synthetic cortisol like prednisone
• Alcohol
• Overtraining
