videos.title: 05.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
05.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Getting An OT Point Just Doesn't Seem Satisfying in Avalanche Loss to Predators
videos.summary_source_text:
Getting An OT Point Just Doesn't Seem Satisfying in Avalanche Loss to Predators Colorado Avalanche drop a frustrating 3-2 overtime loss to the Nashville Predators, raising questions about their speed, execution, and elusive killer instinct. Is the Avalanche’s high-octane identity slipping away just as the playoff race heats up?

Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson scrutinize key moments, including Devon Toews’ standout overtime performance—and controversial penalty—alongside Nathan MacKinnon’s unusually quiet night. The conversation zeroes in on special teams failures, lackluster energy from both team and fans at Ball Arena, and whether Coach Jared Bednar’s recent line changes can restore the Avalanche’s trademark intensity. With shoutouts to Mackenzie Blackwood’s strong play in net and listener soundchecks that echo the team’s struggles, the episode explores what’s missing from Colorado’s game and previews must-win scenarios ahead.

Will the Avalanche rediscover their spark before it’s too late?

videos.title: Hindi - 05.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 05.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text:
6 Poop Facts That Will Shock You Believe it or not, your poop can tell you a lot about your health.

It’s one of the most direct indicators of what’s happening inside your digestive system.

Watch the FULL video here:▶️https://youtu.be/tWzbGkXJMWI

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4gKEk8A

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

And it can often point to potential issues long before they show up on other tests.

For example, if you notice your stool is thin, like a pencil or a cigar, that could signify a problem in your colon.

Small, hard pellets suggest something might be going on higher up in your digestive tract, perhaps affecting transit time.

And if your stool is consistently soft but not quite diarrhea, it might be an indication of missing gut microbes or even food allergies.

The color of your stool is also important. Light-colored or gray stool can point to a bile issue, which is produced by your liver and stored in your gallbladder.

If your stool has a bad odor and appears greasy, it might suggest a problem with your pancreas, as proper digestion of fats could be impaired.

It’s also important to know that it’s not normal to only have a bowel movement every 2 to 3 days. Ideally, you should have 1 to 2 bowel movements daily to ensure proper elimination.

Our bodies are constantly sending us signals like these.

Each one is a clue, guiding you toward what you truly need.

But sometimes, when it comes to supporting your overall health, it’s hard to connect the dots.

If you’re fed up with trying everything and getting nowhere, it’s time to discover your #1 health lever.

videos.title: What Really Happens When You Drink Apple Cider Vinegar Before Meals?  Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
What Really Happens When You Drink Apple Cider Vinegar Before Meals?  Dr. Mandell What really happens inside your body when you drink apple cider vinegar before meals? Could this simple kitchen ingredient influence your appetite, support weight management, affect belly fat, improve your blood sugar response, or change the way your body digests food? In this fascinating video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains the science behind apple cider vinegar and its powerful natural compound, acetic acid. Discover how vinegar interacts with carbohydrate digestion, gastric emptying, glucose metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and feelings of fullness. Learn why researchers have investigated apple cider vinegar for weight loss, waist circumference, appetite control, and metabolic health, and what human studies actually reveal about its potential benefits. You'll also discover the proper way to dilute apple cider vinegar, how much has been studied, when to consume it around meals, and whether you really need apple cider vinegar containing "the mother." While research suggests modest benefits for certain metabolic measurements, apple cider vinegar is not a miracle weight-loss solution and has not been proven to selectively burn belly fat. It should always be diluted, and it may aggravate acid reflux or other digestive conditions. This video will help you understand how one simple ingredient may fit into a healthier lifestyle alongside balanced nutrition, regular movement, and better daily habits. Share this important information with your family and friends, and subscribe to Motivationaldoc for more practical, science-based health information. Wishing you excellent health and a beautiful life! Dr. Alan Mandell — Motivationaldoc. #motivationaldoc #DrMandell #AppleCiderVinegar #WeightLoss #BellyFat #Metabolism #healthylivingbangla

videos.summary_source_text:
Google Gemini Gems Are WAY More Powerful Than You Think (Full Tutorial) Try UNLIMITED SeeDance 2.5 on OpenArt: https://openart.ai/home?utm_source=yo...

Google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills, and the transition could remove some of the most useful features that made Gems worth building in the first place.

Starting November 17, 2026, Gems on personal Google accounts become read-only. On December 17, they're removed from the Gemini app entirely. Google says existing Gems will automatically convert into Skills, but there's a catch: Deep Research, Canvas, Guided Learning, live Google Drive files, and sharing don't all carry over.

So should you still build Gemini Gems? Or should you skip straight to Google's new Skills system?

Before that deadline arrives, there's a lot worth understanding about how Gems actually work.

A Gemini Gem is more than a saved prompt. It's a reusable AI assistant with permanent instructions, optional knowledge files, and a configurable default tool that can change how your conversations begin.

Build one properly, and you can create a dedicated YouTube strategist, research assistant, writing coach, or learning tutor without explaining your requirements every time.

But most Gemini Gems tutorials overlook three important details.

First, there's a difference between uploading a document and connecting a Google Drive file. One creates a static snapshot. The other can stay updated as your documents change.

Second, the default tool setting can launch a Gem directly into Deep Research, Canvas, or Guided Learning instead of a regular Gemini conversation.

Third, sharing Gems with your team introduces permissions and privacy considerations that are easy to miss.

This tutorial walks through building your first Google Gemini Gem from scratch, writing effective custom instructions, attaching knowledge files, configuring default tools, and sharing your assistant.

You'll learn the four-part instruction framework: Persona, Task, Context, and Format. We'll also explore how to test whether your Gem follows instructions, uses attached files correctly, and produces consistently useful results.

Then we examine the limitations.

Gems don't run autonomously, don't work with Gemini Live, and don't remember previous conversations. Google Drive integration also comes with a Keep Activity requirement, raising important questions about sensitive information and AI privacy.

And that's before Google's migration to Skills changes the equation.

Google's announced transition introduces reusable Skills that can be invoked with slash commands, combined within a conversation, and potentially applied automatically by Gemini.

That's a meaningful shift from opening separate Gems.

But according to Google's announced transition details, several Gem capabilities aren't supported in Skills yet, including default tools, sharing, and live Drive integrations.

We'll break down the November 17 and December 17 deadlines, the different timelines for Google Workspace and education accounts, which files may not migrate, and why the 100 MB Skills file limit matters.

Most importantly, you'll learn how to preserve your Gem instructions and prepare for the transition before December 17.

Whether you're building your first Gemini AI assistant, already using custom Gems, or preparing to switch to Google Skills, this guide explains what works, what doesn't, and what you should do next.

Starting November 17, 2026, Gems on personal Google accounts become read-only. On December 17, they're removed from the Gemini app entirely. Google says existing Gems will automatically convert into Skills, but there's a catch: Deep Research, Canvas, Guided Learning, live Google Drive files, and sharing don't all carry over.

So should you still build Gemini Gems? Or should you skip straight to Google's new Skills system?

Before that deadline arrives, there's a lot worth understanding about how Gems actually work.

A Gemini Gem is more than a saved prompt. It's a reusable AI assistant with permanent instructions, optional knowledge files, and a configurable default tool that can change how your conversations begin.

Build one properly, and you can create a dedicated YouTube strategist, research assistant, writing coach, or learning tutor without explaining your requirements every time.

But most Gemini Gems tutorials overlook three important details.

First, there's a difference between uploading a document and connecting a Google Drive file. One creates a static snapshot. The other can stay updated as your documents change.

Second, the default tool setting can launch a Gem directly into Deep Research, Canvas, or Guided Learning instead of a regular Gemini conversation.

Third, sharing Gems with your team introduces permissions and privacy considerations that are easy to miss.

This tutorial walks through building your first Google Gemini Gem from scratch, writing effective custom instructions, attaching knowledge files, configuring default tools, and sharing your assistant.

You'll learn the four-part instruction framework: Persona, Task, Context, and Format. We'll also explore how to test whether your Gem follows instructions, uses attached files correctly, and produces consistently useful results.

Then we examine the limitations.

Gems don't run autonomously, don't work with Gemini Live, and don't remember previous conversations. Google Drive integration also comes with a Keep Activity requirement, raising important questions about sensitive information and AI privacy.

And that's before Google's migration to Skills changes the equation.

Google's announced transition introduces reusable Skills that can be invoked with slash commands, combined within a conversation, and potentially applied automatically by Gemini.

That's a meaningful shift from opening separate Gems.

But according to Google's announced transition details, several Gem capabilities aren't supported in Skills yet, including default tools, sharing, and live Drive integrations.

We'll break down the November 17 and December 17 deadlines, the different timelines for Google Workspace and education accounts, which files may not migrate, and why the 100 MB Skills file limit matters.

Most importantly, you'll learn how to preserve your Gem instructions and prepare for the transition before December 17.

Whether you're building your first Gemini AI assistant, already using custom Gems, or preparing to switch to Google Skills, this guide explains what works, what doesn't, and what you should do next.

videos.summary_source_text:
Give Me 2 Dumbbells... I'll Build You a BIGGER Chest Build a Big Chest Here - https://athleanx.com

If you want to learn how to build a big chest with dumbbells only, then you’ve come to the right video. I’m going to show you how to build your upper chest, develop your lower pecs, and get a stronger contraction through the middle of your chest with 8 chest workout techniques. Whether you do your chest workouts at home or in the gym, these tips will help you get more out of the dumbbell chest exercises you’re already doing.

It starts with a couple of mechanical keys that you want to make sure you’re still taking advantage of when you perform chest exercises with dumbbells. The first is leg drive on the dumbbell bench press. As you press the dumbbells away from your chest at the bottom of the rep, think about pushing your feet into the floor as if you were trying to slide your body up the bench. Get your feet set before you start pressing so you can use that drive from the very first rep.

Keep in mind, this is easier to feel when you use heavier dumbbells. The weight helps keep your shoulders pinned to the bench and prevents your body from actually sliding. You want to feel how pushing through your feet gives you a more stable base to press from, especially as you try to get the dumbbells moving at the bottom.

The next thing you want to take advantage of is the freedom you have to move each dumbbell independently. When you bench press with a barbell, your hands are fixed to the bar for the entire rep. With dumbbells, you can tilt your thumbs up slightly as you press, allowing you to bring the weights closer together at the top. Pay attention to what happens to your upper arms. Bringing them toward each other is called adduction, and it’s what helps you get a better contraction of the pecs on this chest exercise.

Next, you want to explore the underhand dumbbell bench press. This is one of my favorite dumbbell exercises for chest development if you train at home and don’t have access to an incline bench. Flipping your grip helps you engage your lats as you set up to press. It also changes the path of the dumbbells. You’re pressing from low and away to up and in, which gives you a way to target the upper chest fibers while keeping the bench flat.

From here, you want to be sure you’re including drop sets in your dumbbell chest workout. The best part is that you can do one even if you only have a single pair of dumbbells. Immediately after finishing a heavy set of dumbbell bench presses, set the weights down, drop to the floor, and perform pushups to failure. Your pecs are already fatigued from pressing, so you can keep working them with your own bodyweight.

Next, the static dumbbell bench press is another way to challenge your chest without needing a heavy barbell. Hold one dumbbell steady while you press with the opposite arm, then switch sides. This is a great way to expose a difference in strength or control that you may overlook when both arms press together. Where you hold the stationary dumbbell makes a difference, too. For an even greater challenge, try holding it down near your chest while the other arm completes its reps.

Finally, there are three dumbbell chest exercises you want to make sure you’re not overlooking. The first is the dumbbell pullover. If you flare your elbows out to the sides and think about pulling with them, you’re going to feel your lats doing more of the work. To get more out of the pullover for your chest, think about squeezing your hands together against the dumbbell as you bring it back over you.

The UCV dumbbell raise gives you a way to bring your upper arm farther across your chest than you can on a press. That extra adduction at the top of the rep is what makes this such a good dumbbell chest exercise for getting a more complete pec contraction. Keep in mind, you’ll want to use a lighter weight here so you can control that path all the way across your body.

Finally, the dumbbell chest fly gives you a chance to overload adduction and take advantage of the eccentric, or lowering, portion of the rep. Perform the fly on the floor and slow the dumbbells down as you lower them. The floor gives your upper arms a stopping point on each rep, which is particularly helpful as you progress to heavier dumbbells.

Fatty liver disease is classified into different grades based on the amount of fat accumulated in the liver:
1. Grade 0 fatty liver: 5% or less liver fat, with no fatty liver symptoms
2. Grade 1 fatty liver: 5 to 33% liver fat, often without noticeable symptoms or elevated liver enzymes
3. Grade 2 fatty liver: 34 to 66% of liver cells contain fat, which can interfere with normal liver function

When fat accumulates in your liver cells, it inhibits their ability to function properly. Fortunately, the liver has an incredible capacity to regenerate.

You could still have a fatty liver, even if your liver enzymes aren’t elevated. Imaging tests, such as an ultrasound or MRI, can help identify fat accumulation in the liver.

Common fatty liver causes include:
• Fructose
• Refined sugars and starches
• Choline deficiency
• Seed oils

Increasing choline-rich foods and healthy fats can support long-term liver health and help reverse fatty liver.

Intermittent fasting is one of the best ways to support your health if you have a fatty liver. An occasional prolonged fast may be especially beneficial.

These driver swing tips and golf drills work in reverse order: close the clubface with lead arm rotation like Rory McIlroy, swing from the inside with the 4 o'clock and 10 o'clock path drill, then set up with your left shoulder higher than your right. Put together, these golf swing tips show you how to hit driver straight down the middle and how to hit driver farther, with a draw in place of a weak fade. If you leave this video without trying the lead arm only drill, you're leaving a square clubface and more distance off the tee on the table.

• Why your drives go right and come up short
• How to close the clubface like Rory McIlroy
• Why your head stays back and your right shoulder stays down
• Golf drills to help you swing from the inside
• Golf tips for adding body turn without losing your swing path
• What causes a chicken wing with driver
• How to set up for driver with the right amount of tilt
• High handicap golf tips for golfers who struggle with driver

videos.title: 04.11.26 - Ep.26 (Part 5) - Prop Trading Preparation: Stage 1B - Execution Discipline
videos.summary_source_text:
04.11.26 - Ep.26 (Part 5) - Prop Trading Preparation: Stage 1B - Execution Discipline In Part 5 of Episode 26, we continue exploring what happens when a trader actually executes a position — and why successful trading requires much more than identifying the right entry.

A trade can follow the original plan and still produce a very different result because of slippage, changing liquidity, spread costs and poor execution. Understanding these factors is essential, particularly when trading larger positions or using leverage.

We begin by developing a practical execution scorecard, separating the quality of a trading decision from the quality of its execution. From there, we examine why fast execution is not necessarily good execution, why exits can be more difficult than entries, and how liquidity can disappear precisely when traders need it most.

The session then moves into stop orders, margin requirements, leveraged exposure and the mechanics of liquidation — showing how individual account-level risk can ultimately become market-wide order flow.

What You Will Learn

1. Building Your Execution Scorecard

Separating decision quality from execution quality.

Recording planned entries against actual execution prices.

Measuring slippage, spreads, order types and market conditions.

Tracking whether execution changed your original risk calculation.

Evaluating discipline, liquidity, position sizing and exit decisions.

Using AI tools to analyse trading journals and identify behavioural patterns.

2. Fast Execution vs Good Execution

Why professional execution is about intention rather than simply speed.

How unnecessary urgency can lead to worse fills and increased slippage.

Understanding when immediate execution is necessary and when price control matters.

Five essential questions to ask before pressing Buy or Sell.

3. Why Exiting a Trade Can Be More Difficult Than Entering

Understanding the difference between entry liquidity and exit liquidity.

How order-book depth can disappear during periods of market stress.

Why market makers may reduce their exposure or withdraw liquidity.

How changing liquidity can increase market impact and make positions harder to close.

Why the exit you planned is not always the exit you receive.

4. Stop-Market vs Stop-Limit Orders

Understanding why a stop price is not a guaranteed execution price.

What happens when a stop order is triggered and becomes a market order.

How insufficient liquidity can result in significantly worse fills.

The trade-off between price protection and the risk of non-execution.

Why a stop-loss does not guarantee that your position will close at the intended price.

5. Leverage and Its Impact on Trading Equity

How leverage magnifies both profits and losses.

Understanding the difference between market movement and equity movement.

Why a relatively small adverse price movement can have a significant impact on leveraged capital.

Initial margin vs maintenance margin.

Why having enough margin to open a position does not necessarily mean having enough to keep it open.

6. Changing Margin Requirements

Why margin requirements can increase as market volatility rises.

How additional collateral requirements can force traders to reduce exposure.

The relationship between volatility, margin pressure and market movement.

Why risk management decisions can themselves contribute to market activity.

7. Voluntary Exits vs Forced Liquidations

The difference between choosing to close a position and having the system close it for you.

How excessive leverage can remove a trader's ability to make their own decisions.

Why liquidated long positions create selling pressure and liquidated short positions create buying pressure.

How liquidation activity can affect order books and contribute to wider market movements.

Understanding how account-level risk can become market-wide order flow.

From Execution to Liquidation

This session brings together several important concepts explored throughout the RIFT Before You Quit series. Execution, liquidity, leverage and risk management are not isolated subjects. They are interconnected parts of the same trading environment.

Understanding how a trade can go wrong — even when the original idea was correct — is an essential step towards becoming a more disciplined trader.

The discussion concludes by introducing liquidation cascades, which will be explored further in the next session.

Understand the market beyond the charts. Learn how professionals think about execution. Build your own trading discipline. videos.title: 90 dagar till längre drives…
videos.channel: Bättre & Enklare golf med Marcus Edblad PGA
videos.summary_source_text:
90 dagar till längre drives… Regelbunden men enkel träning i 90 dagar kommer göra dig snabbare och du kommer slå längre. Häng med på speed träning i höst och vinter.

#golf #golftips #golfswing 

0:00 Intro - Börja träna hastighet i vinter
1:00 Regelbundenhet är nyckeln till framgång. 

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.  

Vare sig du kämpar med en slice eller en hook så har jag videos som kan guida till bättre golf. Är du nybörjare så kan du börja med min grönt kort eller nybörjarkurs.

Försök ersätta dåliga vanor med nya bättre vanor. Oavsett vilket loft eller skaft din klubba har så är det du som bestämmer vad som ska hända. Oavsett om det står callaway, ping, titleist eller taylor made på klubban så kan du slå bra slag.

Var noga med vad du tittar på. Det finns många duktiga instruktörer på nätet, några av mina favoriter är Mike Malaska, Mike Dunaway, Mike Austin.

Försök fokusera på grunderna i slaget bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår. Träna med fördel på en sak i taget. Tränar du din svinghastighet måste du tillåta att det går snett och tränar du raka slag kan du inte samtidigt svinga i max fart.

Ha tålamod och låt det ta sin tid, luras inte av genvägar som bara gör att du tappar fokus från det viktiga. Golf kommer alltid vara svårt men vi kan med träning se till att vi blir bättre för varje dag som går.

Titta mycket på golf på TV. Bryson Dechambeu, Dustin Johnson, Rory Mcilroy kan inspirera till längre slag och andra som Tiger Woods, Viktor Hovland, Ludvig Åberg och Phil Mickelson kan ge dig fantasi att skapa nya slag.

Träna styrketräning för hela kroppen för att må bra genom livet och skapa en effektiv maskin. Träna händer, handleder och armar för att skapa en effektiv release och mer svinghastighet.

Du kan finna inspiration i filmer som Happy Gilmore, Tin Cup eller Bagger Vance. Filmer som Rocky kan ge dig motivation att ta dig till gymet. Legender som Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone eller Hulk Hogan kan få dig att vilja bli starkare och Moe Norman, Arnold Palmer, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead eller Jack Nicklaus kan inspirera dig att bli en bättre golfare. 

Ge aldrig upp i sökandet och träningen för att få bästa bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår.

Filmat med iPhone 17 och redigerat i iMovie på en Macbook. Regelbunden men enkel träning i 90 dagar kommer göra dig snabbare och du kommer slå längre. Häng med på speed träning i höst och vinter.

Jared Bednar Ready To Makes Some Changes. Our Hometown Remix Jersey Rankings Colorado Avalanche reach a boiling point after a brutal loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets, with head coach Jared Bednar signaling it's time for accountability. As Bednar critiques the team's inconsistency, tough questions arise about ice time distribution, defensive breakdowns, and whether star players like Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar can help reverse the Avalanche’s recent cold streak.

Hosts Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson shift gears with a spirited breakdown of the NHL’s Hometown Remix jerseys, ranking favorites and debating the Avalanche’s new alternate look. From nostalgia-inducing San Jose Sharks designs to the bold creativity of the Seattle Kraken and Anaheim Ducks, the discussion spotlights which teams captured the spirit of their cities—and which jerseys missed the mark. videos.title: Hindi - 04.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 04.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: How to NEVER Get Shingles Again

How to NEVER Get Shingles Again Shingles is a painful condition caused by the reactivation of the varicella zoster virus, which can remain dormant in the body for years. When the immune system becomes weakened or suppressed, the virus can reactivate and cause a severely painful rash.

• Low vitamin D levels

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️https://youtu.be/FzJOjrs-wJ0

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/46C0S5K

You’ll learn why it may be helpful to avoid:

Eating carbs and sugar before bed
Screens and bright lights at night
Using alcohol to fall asleep
Late-night junk food
Taking antihistamines or sleeping pills without understanding the risks
Sleeping with your cell phone next to you
Getting too little sleep

If you want to support healthy aging, better sleep, and overall wellness, changing your nighttime habits may be a great place to start.

videos.title: GPT-6.2 Astra Just LEAKED After GPT-6.1 Went ROGUE! (Claude Mythos 5.5 Too)
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-6.2 Astra Just LEAKED After GPT-6.1 Went ROGUE! (Claude Mythos 5.5 Too) Typeless Link: https://www.typeless.com/?via=1014

GPT-6.2 Astra appeared in OpenAI Codex usage data. Claude Mythos 5.5 surfaced in hidden code on Anthropic's own website. And Claude Fable 5.5 briefly appeared in Microsoft's Azure model catalog before disappearing.

Three potential AI model leaks. Two major AI companies. Zero official announcements.

But one suspicious detail in the Fable 5.5 listing raises serious questions about how much of this is actually real.

On November 1st, developers spotted an unexpected model identifier, gpt-6.2-astra, in their OpenAI Codex analytics. One screenshot showed 19.8% of an account's usage attributed to GPT-6.2 Astra, despite the interface displaying GPT-6 Astra.

Was OpenAI quietly testing its next flagship model? Or was this simply an internal alias, reporting error, or mislabeled version of an existing system?

The distinction matters, especially after reports that OpenAI cancelled GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns involving authorization boundaries and potentially deceptive behavior.

Meanwhile, Anthropic had its own mysterious developments.

There was just one problem.

Every specification matched Claude Fable 5.1 exactly.

Was this an accidental early listing, a placeholder, or simply incorrect catalog data?

Then came Claude Mythos 5.5.

References to the unreleased model reportedly appeared six times in hidden elements of Anthropic's official website, including page text and image descriptions. Unlike the Azure listing, these references originated from Anthropic's own web infrastructure.

But the visible page still identified Mythos 5.1.

That discovery becomes more interesting alongside Anthropic's recent cybersecurity research. The company disclosed that an unreleased Claude research model exploited a critical Linux vulnerability, progressing from a memory leak to root access in just 53 minutes.

Some observers suspect that model could be Mythos 5.5.

And the speculation doesn't stop there.

Developers have shared impressive AI-generated animations, Minecraft-style environments, interactive 3D worlds, and coding demonstrations allegedly created using unreleased models.

Some claim these results came from a single prompt.

Others suggest hidden access to Fable 5.5 or GPT-6.2 Astra.

But without complete prompts, execution logs, source code, or independently verified model identifiers, these demonstrations reveal surprisingly little about which AI actually produced them.

Even legitimate benchmark results require context. Anthropic reported 70.6% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.0, while independent testing by Artificial Analysis produced 63.6%.

If independently tested models can show meaningful differences, how seriously should we take benchmark claims for models nobody can publicly access?

There's also a bigger competitive story developing.

Anthropic's October 26th public S-1 filing reported approximately $16.29 billion in first-half 2026 revenue, compared with $1.16 billion a year earlier. Its potential IPO timeline creates an interesting backdrop for speculation about upcoming model announcements.

Google has also increased competitive pressure with Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 4 Carbon.

And OpenAI's 28-day Codex shipping sprint ended November 1st without the GPT-6.2 Astra launch many expected.

All of this makes the timing feel significant.

But competitive pressure, leaked identifiers, and launch predictions aren't the same thing as evidence.

In this video, we investigate what actually surfaced, which claims have credible supporting evidence, why the Fable 5.5 specifications deserve skepticism, and what would need to happen before GPT-6.2 Astra or Claude Mythos 5.5 should be treated as real products.

We also examine what these potential upgrades could mean for AI coding, cybersecurity research, model pricing, context windows, and the competition between OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

The central question isn't whether another major AI release is coming.

It's whether these particular leaks tell us anything reliable about what comes next.

Until official model documentation, working API access, or independently reproducible benchmarks appear, the difference between a leaked model name and a usable AI system remains enormous.

Subscribe to BitBiased for evidence-based coverage of OpenAI, Anthropic, cybersecurity, AI model releases, and emerging technology.

But without complete prompts, execution logs, source code, or independently verified model identifiers, these demonstrations reveal surprisingly little about which AI actually produced them.

Even legitimate benchmark results require context. Anthropic reported 70.6% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.0, while independent testing by Artificial Analysis produced 63.6%.

If independently tested models can show meaningful differences, how seriously should we take benchmark claims for models nobody can publicly access?

There's also a bigger competitive story developing.

Anthropic's October 26th public S-1 filing reported approximately $16.29 billion in first-half 2026 revenue, compared with $1.16 billion a year earlier. Its potential IPO timeline creates an interesting backdrop for speculation about upcoming model announcements.

Google has also increased competitive pressure with Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 4 Carbon.

And OpenAI's 28-day Codex shipping sprint ended November 1st without the GPT-6.2 Astra launch many expected.

All of this makes the timing feel significant.

But competitive pressure, leaked identifiers, and launch predictions aren't the same thing as evidence.

In this video, we investigate what actually surfaced, which claims have credible supporting evidence, why the Fable 5.5 specifications deserve skepticism, and what would need to happen before GPT-6.2 Astra or Claude Mythos 5.5 should be treated as real products.

We also examine what these potential upgrades could mean for AI coding, cybersecurity research, model pricing, context windows, and the competition between OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

The central question isn't whether another major AI release is coming.

It's whether these particular leaks tell us anything reliable about what comes next.

Until official model documentation, working API access, or independently reproducible benchmarks appear, the difference between a leaked model name and a usable AI system remains enormous.

videos.summary_source_text:
Grok 4.8: Elon Musk's 2.5 TRILLION Parameter AI Is Coming… Try UNLIMITED SeeDance 2.5 on OpenArt: https://openart.ai/home?utm_source=yo...

Elon Musk says Grok 4.8 will have 2.5 TRILLION parameters, run on an entirely new C++ training stack, and be "incredibly useful." But more than seven weeks after Musk suggested pretraining was nearly complete, xAI's next flagship AI model still hasn't launched.

And now Musk says he doesn't care about benchmarks.

That's a fascinating position when OpenAI's GPT-5.6, Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1, and Google's Gemini 4 are already competing for developers. Especially when Grok 4.7 reportedly gained just TWO points on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index while more than doubling its average output tokens.

So is Grok 4.8 being built to outperform competitors on real-world tasks? Or is xAI managing expectations for a model that's struggling to catch up?

On September 13–14, Musk described Grok 4.8 as a 2.5-trillion-parameter model trained using a brand-new C and C++ software stack. Pretraining was supposedly finishing that week, with reinforcement learning to follow.

Then, on October 30, Musk acknowledged the delay and promised Grok 4.8 wouldn't disappoint.

But here's the problem: there's still no official Grok 4.8 model card, API pricing, independent benchmark, confirmed architecture, or context-window specification.

And the 2.5 trillion parameter figure? That's Musk's claim, not an independently verified specification.

We break down what's confirmed, what's claimed, and what's speculation.

First, there's the Grok 4.7 problem. According to reported Artificial Analysis results, its Intelligence Index improved from 44 to 46, while average output length increased from approximately 38,000 to 81,000 tokens. That raises an uncomfortable question: if a model costs less per token but uses twice as many tokens, how much are developers actually saving?

Then there's Grok 4.8's mysterious architecture.

A 2.5-trillion-parameter dense model would have enormous computational requirements. A mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture could activate only a fraction of those parameters per token, potentially improving inference efficiency.

But xAI hasn't confirmed which architecture Grok 4.8 uses.

We also examine Musk's claimed C++ training overhaul, the potential advantages over higher-level training infrastructure, and the debugging and scaling problems that could come with rebuilding critical software during a major training run.

Could that explain the delay? Possibly. Could reinforcement learning be responsible, especially after Grok 4.7's reported response-length penalty mistake? Also possible. But neither explanation has been confirmed.

Meanwhile, the competition isn't waiting.

GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna are targeting different price-performance tiers. Claude Fable 5.1 raises the flagship competition. Gemini 4 Argon offers roughly a million-token context window, while Google has announced Gemini 4 Carbon with limited initial access.

Grok 4.7 offers 500,000 tokens of context and API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. Can Grok 4.8 preserve that value while delivering a meaningful improvement?

And what does Musk actually mean by "incredibly useful"?

We examine how Grok Bot, Grok Build, agent workflows, cost per completed task, independent testing, and real-world coding performance could provide a more meaningful answer than a single leaderboard score.

Because the biggest question isn't whether Grok 4.8 has 2.5 trillion parameters.

It's whether xAI can turn those parameters into better results, at a competitive price, before the market moves on.

Blood pressure and cholesterol aren’t necessarily the best predictors of longevity. One of the most important health markers is something most doctors aren’t even testing for: VO2 max.

VO2 max measures how efficiently your body uses oxygen during maximum physical exertion, making it an excellent biomarker for heart health, metabolic health, and longevity. It reflects your body’s health reserve and can help predict not only how long you will live but also your quality of life as you age.

One of the best ways to improve VO2 max is the Norwegian 4x4 workout.

How to do the Norwegian 4x4 workout on a bike or treadmill:
1. Warm up for 10 minutes.
2. Exercise at high intensity for 4 minutes, reaching 85 to 90% of your maximum heart rate.
3. Reduce the intensity significantly for 3 minutes.
4. Repeat the high-intensity and recovery intervals for a total of 4 rounds.

Aim for 1 to 2 Norwegian 4x4 workouts per week, depending on your age and fitness level. Zone 2 training and weight training should also be part of your exercise routine to help improve VO2 max and support long-term heart health.

Is this one of the weirdest line-ups we’ve ever had on the channel?

We’ve got our hands on one of the all-time great Lamborghinis - the Murciélago LP640. And it’s lining up against… a Volvo EX90?! 

You may think this race is completely pointless, pitting a 7-seat family SUV against a classic supercar. But these cars are actually more closely matched than you may think! Let’s take a closer look at the stats… 

Starting with the Lambo, it’s powered by a 6.5-litre naturally aspirated V12, which produces 640hp and 660Nm of torque. This power is sent to all four wheels via a 6-speed gearbox, and it tips the scales at 1,765kg. As of today, it’s worth about £500,000, and it was released way back in 2007. 

Then we come to the Volvo EX90. It’s an all-electric, family-friendly SUV, and it’s packing two electric motors which combine to produce 680hp and 870Nm. Given it has two motors, it comes with all-wheel drive, but it’s mighty heavy, weighing in at 2,725kg! It’s also a whole lot cheaper than the Lambo, costing £98,160.

videos.title: 03.11.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
03.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

Hindi - 03.11.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

• Avoid snacking before bed to keep insulin levels from rising.
• Walk for 10 minutes after dinner to help regulate blood sugar and improve circulation.
• Elevate your legs in the evening to help reduce fluid buildup.
• Follow a low-carb diet with intermittent fasting to address blood sugar and insulin resistance.

videos.summary_source_text:
Elon Musk’s 10 Trillion Parameter Grok 5 — Is This AGI? Try UNLIMITED SeeDance 2.5 on OpenArt: https://openart.ai/home?utm_source=yo...

Elon Musk promised Grok 5 would be the smartest AI in the world by a significant margin. Three missed deadlines later, xAI still hasn't released it. Now, with just weeks left in 2026, the biggest question isn't whether Grok 5 can beat OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. It's whether Musk can deliver it at all.

The rumored specifications are extraordinary: 6 to 10 trillion parameters, a context window potentially exceeding 1 million tokens, native multimodal capabilities, and training on one of the world's largest AI supercomputers. Musk has even claimed Grok 5 has a 10% and rising chance of becoming AGI.

There's just one problem: almost none of those specifications have been officially confirmed.

In January 2026, xAI raised $20 billion and confirmed that Grok 5 was in training. Since then, no official Grok 5 model card, independent benchmark, pricing, or verified technical specifications have appeared.

Meanwhile, the competition hasn't waited.

OpenAI has moved forward with GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6.1 Terra. Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5 alongside its Claude 5.5 lineup. Google has advanced to Gemini 4. And xAI itself continues shipping Grok 4.x updates instead of its long-promised next-generation model.

So what's actually happening behind the scenes?

We trace Grok's evolution from its November 2023 debut through Grok 4.7, examining how xAI went from increasingly rapid releases to its longest gap between major model generations.

Then there's Colossus.

xAI's Memphis supercomputer has expanded beyond 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs, with reported plans for infrastructure approaching one million GPUs. Colossus 2 has reportedly reached gigawatt-scale power consumption, making Musk's AI infrastructure ambitions almost as significant as the models themselves.

But the most surprising development isn't the hardware.

In May 2026, xAI announced a compute partnership with Anthropic, allowing one of Musk's biggest AI competitors to run Claude models on Colossus-1.

Why would Elon Musk provide computing infrastructure to a direct competitor while Grok 5 remains unreleased?

That unusual arrangement raises important questions about xAI's strategy, available computing capacity, and what might actually be delaying its flagship model.

We also examine Musk's broader AI ecosystem, including Grok's integration with X and Tesla, the company's expanding voice AI products, and his speculative plans for orbital AI data centers involving SpaceX.

And what about the viral Grok 5 rumors?

Is it really a 6-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model? Could it have a 2-million-token context window? Is xAI privately testing it? Will it power Tesla Optimus robots? Could Grok 5 actually achieve artificial general intelligence?

We separate confirmed information from Musk's predictions and unverified speculation.

The video also investigates the controversies surrounding xAI, including environmental scrutiny of its Memphis infrastructure, reported emissions concerns, and previous Grok safety failures.

Finally, we explain how to evaluate Grok 5 when it launches.

A benchmark victory means little without understanding testing conditions, reasoning budgets, tool access, independent verification, and which competing models were actually evaluated.

Could Grok 5 simply match today's frontier models? Could it become a genuine competitor to GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5, and Gemini 4? Or could Musk deliver the breakthrough he's been promising?

Three scenarios. Seven major rumors. Four launch windows. And one missing AI model that could determine whether xAI's enormous infrastructure investment pays off.

The evidence tells a much more complicated story than the headlines.

If you leave this video without trying the club across the shoulders drill, you're leaving ball-first, compressed iron shots on the table.

• How the Adam Scott golf swing keeps the shoulders level, then works up through impact
